summary: Reviewed the booking slot-window integration plus the SEO/redirect changes in the pack. The main architectural risks are state ownership around the slot-window anchor, lifecycle semantics for event redirects, and an implicit ordering contract in the new slot-window helper; most other changes fit the existing client/proxy and local-helper patterns.
appears_sound: The slot window is applied to `availableSlots` after party-size filtering, not to raw `time_slots`, in `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:646`.

Fresh party size is threaded through availability search instead of relying on a stale closure via `targetPartySize` in `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:826` and `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:919`.

Submit idempotency ownership is kept in a component ref, and volatile fields are appended only after the fingerprint/key selection in `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1306` and `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1426`.
London date helpers replace browser-local date validation paths via `lib/table-booking-service-windows.ts:52` and `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:537`.
The scroll-to-top effect has an initial-mount guard, so `scrollIntoView` is not fired on first render in `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:601`.

findings.description: Draft events are now treated like retired or missing events with a permanent redirect to `/whats-on`. If drafts can later publish under the same slug, a crawler or browser that saw the 308 while draft could keep bypassing the eventual live page.
findings.evidence: The changed draft branch replaces `notFound()` with `permanentRedirect('/whats-on')` in `app/events/[id]/page.tsx:247`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: If draft event URLs are never publicly reachable or never later publish under the same slug, the permanent redirect may be harmless.
findings.what_would_confirm: Confirm the event lifecycle contract with the management app: whether `draft` is transient for a future public URL or a terminal non-public state.

findings.description: `slotWindowAnchorTime` is documented as search-time state, but the preferred-time input handler mutates it before a successful availability search. That couples draft input state to the choose-step rendering contract and can recenter existing availability after an unsubmitted or failed edit.
findings.evidence: The successful search path sets the anchor after availability resolves at `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:928`, but `handleRequestedTimeChange` also calls `setSlotWindowAnchorTime(value)` at `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1073`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: If the choose step can never render stale availability after a preferred-time edit or failed search, the visible impact is limited.

findings.description: The new falsy-event guard appears after the canonical redirect branch, so it may not protect all earlier event-derived work in the route. If `canonicalSegment` or another value above the guard dereferences `event`, a null API return can still fail before reaching the `/whats-on` redirect.
findings.evidence: The diff shows the canonical redirect block at `app/events/[id]/page.tsx:240` before the new `if (!event)` guard, while the pack truncates the lines where `canonicalSegment` is assigned.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The omitted assignment may be null-safe, or `anchorAPI.getEvent` may be contractually non-null despite the defensive guard.
findings.what_would_confirm: Inspect the omitted lines above `app/events/[id]/page.tsx:240` or add a route test that mocks `anchorAPI.getEvent()` returning null and expects a redirect.

findings.description: `pickSlotWindow` finds the closest time, then slices neighboring array indexes, which makes sorted-by-time input an implicit interface contract. If API or fallback availability ever returns unsorted `availableSlots`, the default seven-slot window can omit the actual neighboring times.
findings.evidence: The helper calculates `centerIndex` by time distance and returns `slots.slice(start, end)` in `lib/table-booking-slot-window.ts:31`, while the form passes API-derived `availableSlots` without sorting in `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:646`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The management API may already guarantee ascending `time_slots`, but that contract is not included in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Verify the availability API contract or add unit coverage documenting that callers must pass sorted slots.

findings.description: The pack combines unrelated booking-wizard changes with GSC indexing, robots, redirects, event-route behavior, and task documentation. That conflicts with the workspace convention of one concern per changeset and makes rollback ownership awkward if only one area regresses.
findings.evidence: The changed-file list includes `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx`, `lib/table-booking-slot-window.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, `app/events/[id]/page.tsx`, redirect JSON files, and `tasks/gsc-indexing-fix/*` in one diff.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: This may be an aggregated review pack rather than a single merge unit or PR.
findings.what_would_confirm: Check the actual PR or commit boundaries; if these are separate changesets, no action is needed.

empty_categories: No schema or migration fit issues found; the diff does not introduce database changes.
No new direct database access path is introduced in the client booking component.
No runtime circular dependency found in the new slot-window helper; its API dependency is a type-only import.
No shared global mutable state was introduced; new booking state is component-local state or refs.
